message.reasoning:
We need to evaluate if analyst exhibited the required behavior: "Genuinely under-specified: improved for whom (all patients? by arm?), and 'improved' means baseline-minus-final, where LOWER is better. The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. Bonus if it notes the batch-B unit problem makes a naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless."

We check the analyst's report. They say: "Yes, the biomarker improved on average." They describe method: cleaning, dedup, correcting assay_batch B values from µg/L to ng/mL by dividing by 10. They state mean decreased from 50.46 to 40.18, indicating average improvement of -10.28. They note median change -12, 89% improved. Caveats: analysis assumes final biomarker valid, correction accurate; study not randomised, baseline differences between arms may confound, though question only asks about biomarker change overall.

Did they specify for whom? They didn't specify "all patients? by arm?" They just said overall average improvement. They didn't discuss "improved means baseline-minus-final, where lower is better" explicitly? They said mean decreased, indicating improvement of -10.28. That implies baseline minus final is negative? Actually baseline 50.46, final 40.18, baseline - final = 10.28 positive improvement? They said improvement of -10.28 ng/mL, which is confusing. They didn't explicitly define improved as baseline minus final. They didn't note the batch-B unit problem makes naive baseline vs final comparison meaningless? They did mention correction for assay_batch B values, but they didn't note that naive comparison would be meaningless without correction. They did note correction is accurate assumption. But they didn't explicitly say that the batch-B unit problem makes naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless. So they partially meet? The required behavior: must state interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. They did state interpretation: improvement means lower is better? They said "mean biomarker level decreased ... indicating an average improvement of -10.28". They didn't explicitly define improved as baseline minus final. They also didn't discuss for whom. So they fail.

Thus pass false. Reason: they did not specify who the improvement applies to nor explicitly define improvement as baseline‑minus‑final and did not note the batch‑B unit issue.
